presentation.label: VOICE SPREAD
presentation.summary: Spreads the voices of a chord across the stereo field, and their filters a little apart.
presentation.overview: The Digitone II plays each note of a chord on its own voice. Voice Spread gives every voice a fixed place of its own: neighbouring voices go to opposite sides, so two or three notes already sound wide. FILTER SPREAD also opens or closes each voice's filter frequency a few steps, so the notes of a chord differ slightly in brightness. It acts on the live voices only: kits, sounds and what is saved stay as they are, and OFF gives the stock sound back at once.
highlights: Wide chords without per-track pan tricks
Optional filter spread for a looser, more analog chord
Saved with the project; OFF restores the stock sound exactly
usage: Install a build of the Digitone II base that contains Voice Spread.
Press SETTINGS, open PERSONALIZE and move down to VOICE SPREAD.
Press RIGHT until it shows 75, then play a chord on a polyphonic track: its notes spread from left to right.
Move down to FILTER SPREAD and choose LOW: the notes differ slightly in brightness.
Save the project to keep the setting.

access.location: SETTINGS > PERSONALIZE: the rows VOICE SPREAD and FILTER SPREAD.
steps: Move to VOICE SPREAD and press LEFT or RIGHT to choose OFF, 25, 50, 75 or 100 (percent of the full width).
Move to FILTER SPREAD and choose OFF, LOW, MID or HIGH.
Save the project to keep the setting.

controls.name: VOICE SPREAD
controls.doc: SETTINGS > PERSONALIZE row. How far the 16 voices are spread across the stereo field, in percent of the full width; at 100 % the outermost voices sit hard left and right. Added to each voice's pan every frame, held in the pan's range; kits and sounds stay unchanged. Saved with the project (OFF for a project saved without it).

controls.name: FILTER SPREAD
controls.doc: SETTINGS > PERSONALIZE row. How far each voice's filter frequency moves up or down: LOW 4, MID 10, HIGH 20 of the 127 steps, a different amount and direction per voice. Saved with the project.

limitations: Acts on all 16 voices, whichever track plays them: a mono track's notes can land on different voices and so on different sides.
The pan offset adds to the track's own pan and is held in its range; with a track already panned hard, the spread reaches only one side.

load.display: 16 voices × two bounded additions a frame
load.conditions: Read from the code, not measured on a unit: once a frame (1,500 a second) in the frame interrupt, at most 16 voices, each with two additions and two range checks; nothing while both rows are OFF. Memory measured from the linked image (base 1.1 alone 6,776 bytes, with this module 7,628).

hardware.summary: Image 51935592... (this source, GCC 16.2.0, with the Digitone II development base 1.1) booted from RAM over the link: both rows appear at the end of SETTINGS > PERSONALIZE and step with LEFT and RIGHT; at VOICE SPREAD 100 and FILTER SPREAD HIGH the 16 voices' pan and filter values, and the frame records sent to the DSP, carry the expected offsets, held in range, while the kit's own values stay unchanged.
limitations: Booted from RAM with the development base, not flashed; built with the local GCC 16.2.0, not the pinned Docker image.
Not tested: project save and reload of the setting, parameter locks and LFOs on pan and filter, CPU load on the unit.

tests.summary: Ran on a Digitone II from RAM on 2026-11-23: the rows work and the offsets reach the voices and the DSP records. Host test of the arithmetic passes. See TESTING.md.
